text:
Two cron jobs ran at midnight. Both sent the billing batch. Half our customers got duplicate invoices.

No leader. No lock. Just two healthy servers doing the same "run once" job because both thought they were in charge.

Distributed coordination is hard because processes crash, networks partition, and clocks lie. Leader election picks one writer. Distributed locks gate critical sections — when you really need them.

What I learned the hard way:

• TTL locks without fencing tokens can let a stale holder corrupt data after a pause
• "We'll use Redis SETNX" without expiry → dead lock forever if the holder dies mid-work
• Building your own coordinator when managed consensus exists is a last resort

Sometimes the right fix is "only one scheduler pod" or a queue with single consumer — not a general lock service.

Full post on split-brain, lease renewal, and when not to roll your own.
